BLOCKER: `webhook.go` calls `ResolveHMACKey`, but `go/eventtransport/secrets.go` (declared in design `affected_files`) is absent from the diff → the new package does not compile and its tests cannot run; AC-2 evidence is unverifiable.

No production wiring: `Registry` and the three transports have zero call sites outside tests, and nothing constructs/registers them for `DispatchOnce` → AC-1 (subscriber actually receives events via inproc/webhook/notify with dispatcher retry/DLQ) is not met ("wire fully").
AC-4 observability unmet: no `event_delivery_attempts_total` / retry-age / dlq-depth / latency metrics or redacted logs are emitted anywhere in the diff, including the modified dispatcher path.

FR-3/AC-1 verification gap: the new `IsPermanent` immediate-DLQ branch in `DispatchOnce` has no unit or dispatcher integration test in the diff (the referenced `event_dispatcher_pg_integration_test.go` evidence file is not present).
MAJOR: SSRF bypass: `validateTarget` only blocks literal localhost/private IPs and the string `localhost`; a DNS name resolving to a loopback/private address passes when `PF_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=false`, violating the approved security contract.
Registry provides no tenant scoping: `Get(name)` cannot reject cross-tenant lookup (control C-6), and `TestRegistryTenantLookup` asserts nothing tenant-related.
429 `Retry-After` is not honored (failure matrix requires `retry max(backoff, retry-after)`); 429 is returned as an undifferentiated transient error.

Notify idempotency/ordering: email failure after a successful in-app POST returns an error → dispatcher retry re-POSTs and creates duplicate in-app notifications; the server ignores the `Idempotency-Key` header it sends (FR-2 idempotency unmet).
Email recipient is hard-coded to `SMTP.From` (self): no subscriber/tenant recipient is derived, so the notify/email transport never informs an actual subscriber (AC-3 half-met).

New flags (`PF_WEBHOOK_*`, `PF_NOTIFY_*`, `PF_SMTP_*`) are not declared in `config/env-flags.json` (a declared affected file absent from the diff), and the guardrail "startup validates config shape; missing HMAC disables webhook only" is not implemented (missing key instead DLQs every delivery).

`docs/EVENT-TRANSPORTS-DESIGN.md` (referenced by `gen_docs_index.py` and all traceability evidence) and the traceability test files (`inproc_test.go`, `webhook_test.go`, `notify_test.go`, `registry_test.go`) are missing from the diff.
MINOR: 401/403 returns a plain `fmt.Errorf`, indistinguishable from 5xx in logs/stats; no `AUTH_RETRY` classification/observability per failure matrix.
API response `email_eligible` is computed from a hard-coded `("medium","high","critical")` set and ignores `PF_NOTIFY_EMAIL_MIN_PRIORITY`, so it can disagree with the transport's actual gate.
`create_notification` declares `require_operator` twice (route dependency and `ctx` param) and `ctx` is unused.
`priorityOf` uses substring matching (`strings.Contains(type,"high"/"low")`) — brittle misclassification for unrelated event type names.

Design guardrail "bounded title/message length" is implemented as silent truncation (`title[:200]`, `message[:4000]`) rather than a validation error; `openapi.json` body schema is `additionalProperties: true` with no documented field validation (contract drift).
NIT: `var _ = strings.TrimSpace` dead-code shim in `webhook.go` exists only to justify the `strings` import; contradicts the `no-dead-code` tech-stack evidence.
`products/product_forge/notifications.json` commits generated runtime notification data (future timestamps, missing trailing newline) into the repo.
`test_notifications_api_wrapper.py` uses `importlib` file-loading indirection to re-export tests instead of normal test discovery.
SUMMARY: The change is well-scoped (Go transports, additive endpoint, dispatcher-owned permanent-error DLQ) but is not wired or observable: missing `secrets.go`, an unused registry, no metrics, and no test for the new dispatcher DLQ path mean AC-1/AC-4 and parts of AC-2/AC-3 are not demonstrably met.

Top risks: package build failure, SSRF DNS bypass, duplicate in-app notifications on retry (no server-side idempotency), email sent only to the operator's own address, and undeclared env flags/design docs breaking the config and traceability contracts.
